findings.issue: WEBHOOK_ENCRYPTION_KEY falls back to JWT_SECRET for AES-256-GCM encryption
findings.impact: If WEBHOOK_ENCRYPTION_KEY is not configured, getEncryptionKey() derives AES key from JWT_SECRET via SHA-256. JWT_SECRET is designed for JWT signing, not encryption. Compromise of JWT_SECRET reveals all encrypted webhook secrets. No key rotation mechanism exists.
findings.fix: Make WEBHOOK_ENCRYPTION_KEY required in env schema. Remove JWT_SECRET fallback. Add key rotation support with version-prefixed encrypted values.
findings.exploit_chain: Attacker who obtains JWT_SECRET (via env leak, CI/CD exposure, or SSRF) can decrypt all stored webhook secrets using the derived key. With decrypted secrets, attacker can forge webhook signatures or hijack active webhook endpoints.

findings.issue: Reactions SELECT policy uses using(true) allowing all authenticated users cross-tenant access
findings.impact: Any authenticated user can enumerate reactions (emoji + user_id pairs) on any message across all workspaces. Leaks user activity patterns and workspace relationships.
findings.fix: Replace with scoped policy checking workspace membership via messages -> channels -> workspace_members join chain
findings.exploit_chain: Attacker creates account, authenticates, queries GET /v1/messages/:id/reactions for arbitrary message IDs. Without workspace membership check, they can map user-emoji relationships across the entire platform.

findings.issue: CSP script-src 'self' without nonce or hash blocks Next.js inline hydration scripts
findings.impact: Next.js production builds inject inline script elements for page hydration. Current CSP blocks these, causing frontend JavaScript failure. Forces CSP to be disabled, negating XSS protection.
findings.fix: Add nonce generation in middleware or use 'strict-dynamic' for Next.js compatibility
findings.exploit_chain: Without a working CSP, XSS vulnerabilities in user-generated content become exploitable across all pages.

findings.issue: GET /reactions/batch endpoint lacks message access validation
findings.impact: Batch reactions endpoint accepts arbitrary message_ids without checking user's workspace/channel membership. User can fetch reactions for messages in channels they don't belong to.
findings.fix: Add requireMessageAccess validation or verify each message_id against accessible channels server-side before returning reactions.
findings.exploit_chain: Hitting GET /v1/reactions/batch with message IDs from inaccessible channels returns reaction data, leaking user-emoji associations.

findings.issue: In-memory error buffer may expose sensitive data via admin logs endpoint
findings.impact: Error buffer stores unredacted error messages containing user IDs, IPs, paths. Any admin user can read GET /admin/logs. Buffer limited to 200 entries but sensitive data may accumulate.
findings.fix: Add PII redaction before pushError(). Filter sensitive fields from error entries. Consider time-based TTL.
